title: Automate KMS/HSM TLS rotation for private-installer (Vault + SealedSecrets + Helm + Terraform)
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Automates TLS and KMS/HSM key rotation for private deployments: Vault integration, SealedSecrets reconciliation, Helm chart hooks, Terraform module updates, and safer upgrade/rollback paths.
description:
Motivation: Private (VPC/on-prem) customers need automated, auditable rotation of TLS certificates and KMS keys to satisfy compliance and reduce manual ops. Current private-installer deployments require manual steps for cert renewal and KMS/HSM key refresh which is error-prone during upgrades. This PR implements an end-to-end automation flow: Vault Transit support for key wrapping, HSM-aware key rotation hooks, SealedSecrets reconciliation for secret distribution, Helm chart additions for certificate-rotation controllers, Terraform module variables for rotation scheduling, and upgrade/rollback tooling improvements to ensure safe key changeovers.

What this PR changes (high level):
- private-installer: add a new controller (cert-rotator) packaged as a Helm subchart that watches certificate CRs and triggers rotation workflows. The controller supports dry-run, force-rotate, and pre/post hooks for rollouts.
- Helm charts: new templates for cert-rotator Deployment, ClusterRole/RoleBindings, and ConfigMap-driven rotation policies. Added prober liveness/readiness checks and PodDisruptionBudget to prevent mass restarts during rotation windows.
- Terraform modules: expose new inputs (rotation_schedule_cron, vault_transit_key_name, hsm_key_slot, sealed_secrets_namespace) and outputs (rotation_job_id, last_rotation_timestamp). Add documentation and example usage in the terraform/privatemanifests module.
- Vault integration: add instructions and code to configure Vault Transit as an optional KMS provider. The operator supports online wrapping/unwrapping via transit and a reconciliation loop that validates Vault health before key operations.
- HSM support: HSM integration points (PKCS#11) added to the agent wrapper. Rotation now supports HSM key lifecycle semantics: generate new key, export wrapped key via Vault Transit, and atomically switch references in Kubernetes secrets.
- SealedSecrets: reconcile flow updated so that new sealed payloads are created as part of rotation and old payloads are garbage-collected after successful rollout. This avoids window where secrets are stale.
- Upgrade/Rollback tooling: private-installer upgrade hooks updated to create safe checkpoints: pre-rotation snapshot (etcd + secrets manifest), post-rotation verification suite (smoke tests), and a rollback path that can restore the prior key references with minimal downtime.
- Tests: added unit tests for the rotation controller, integration tests in the private-installer e2e pipeline that exercise Vault/HSM flows (mocked HSM in CI), and canary rollout tests in perf-canary to assert latency/regression does not spike during rotation.

Commits summary:
- Initial controller and Helm templates (Asha)
- Terraform inputs/outputs and example (Asha)
- Vault transit integration (Samir)

CI / checks: All CI pipelines passed on final push. Notable earlier failures: integration tests failed initially due to Vault token TTL handling (fixed by adding token renewal logic in handler_vault.go). Flaky e2e probe timeout was stabilized by adding exponential backoff in rotator readiness probe.

Review conversation (summary):
- Samir: Asked for stronger Vault health gating and a safe-fail path if Vault is unreachable during scheduled rotation; requested documentation for operator behavior under partial failures. Response: added Vault health checks and operator will abort rotation and create an alert/event if Vault is unhealthy.
- Emily: Requested explicit HSM test coverage and PKCS#11 config validation; found a corner case where HSM key generation fails with certain slot permissions. Response: added retries and clearer error messages; added instructions in docs for common vendor HSM setup.
- Liam: Concerned about rollout safety for stateful components; asked to add PDBs and staggered rollouts. Response: implemented PodDisruptionBudget and annotated Deployments to use maxUnavailable=1 for critical components; added canary label support.
- Minor nits: naming of Terraform variables (renamed to more consistent snake_case), comments in controller.go, and docs formatting.

Manual testing and rollout notes:
- Deployed to staging using the new terraform module variables and enabled vault_transit_key_name. Ran a dry-run rotation (cert-rotator --dry-run) to validate the workflow end-to-end.
- Tested HSM flow using a mocked PKCS#11 provider in CI; in customer lab we validated with a SoftHSM instance and one partner HSM vendor.
- Verified that sealed secrets were replaced atomically and that existing pods reloaded secrets via projected volumes (reloader sidecar) during a canary deployment.
- Rollback tested by triggering the private-installer rollback hook which restored the previous secrets manifest and validated that services came back without requiring manual intervention.

Security considerations:
- Vault is treated as the primary key-wrapping authority; the operator never logs unwrapped private key material. All sensitive values are written to sealed secrets and never kept in plain text in CI artifacts.
- Added RBAC rules scoped to the sealed-secrets controller and the rotator. Documentation includes recommended service account policies to limit blast radius.

Documentation and runbooks:
- docs/private-installer/rotation.md includes: Vault setup steps, HSM onboarding guide, rotation scheduling examples, upgrade/rollback playbook, and troubleshooting section with common error messages and remediation.

Backwards compatibility and migration: The rotator is opt-in via values.yaml (rotation.enabled=false by default). Existing private-installer customers will not be affected until they enable the feature and provide KMS/HSM/Vault configuration. Terraform module adds optional variables with sensible defaults.

Follow-ups / future work:
- Add metrics and Grafana dashboards for rotation events and latency (linked work ENG-4402).
- Support for cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS/Azure Key Vault) via a generic provider interface (ENG-4450).
- Improve operator observability: correlation ids and trace propagation into Vault calls.

Merge outcome: Approved by reviewers after 2 rounds of changes. Squash-merged to main on 2026-03-01. Changelog entry added to release notes.
